transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I just haven’t been able to get past what happened. Since my friend was killed, I’ve been carrying this constant mix of guilt, fear, and anger, and it hasn’t eased up the way people seemed to think it would.
Can you tell me more about the event when your friend was killed? Were you present or directly involved in any way?

I’m not sure I can give the details you’re asking for. I know my friend was killed, and that’s what I keep coming back to, but… I don’t know how much more I can say about whether I was there or directly involved.
Since your friend’s death, have you had upsetting memories or flashbacks about it that keep coming back, even when you don’t want them to?

Yes. Certain things set it off before I can even think. A crosswalk signal, the sound of a truck, even looking at one of those walking-tour maps… suddenly the whole scene is back in my head so clearly. I can see my friend stepping off the curb, and I can’t stop it.
Since your friend’s death, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yes. I avoid that intersection completely if I can. I’ll take a longer way around just so I don’t have to pass it.

And I’ve stopped signing up for most tours or safety meetings too, because the conversations always seem to drift back to what happened there, and I just can’t sit through that.
Since your friend’s death, have you noticed any lasting negative beliefs about yourself, others, or the world, or have you experienced persistent negative emotions like guilt, shame, or anger?

Yes. That’s really why I’m here. Since my friend was killed, I’ve been carrying this constant guilt, fear, and anger. It’s just there most of the time.

People seemed to think it would ease up with time, but it hasn’t, not really. It still feels heavy.
Since your friend’s death, have you lost interest in activities or hobbies that used to be important to you?

Yes. I used to really care about my garden, planning the beds and what would bloom when. I quilted with a group of ladies, went to theater outings, and book club used to be something I enjoyed, even the arguing.

Now I see those things on the calendar and I just... don’t feel much. It’s like they’re part of a life I used to have, or someone I used to be.
Since your friend’s death, have you had trouble experiencing positive emotions like happiness or love, or have you felt emotionally numb for extended periods?

I’m not sure. I know I don’t enjoy things the way I used to, but whether that’s numbness exactly… I don’t know.

There are moments I can still feel warmth toward my family, or smile at something small. It’s just not as easy or as steady as it used to be.
Since your friend’s death, have you been more jumpy or easily startled, or found yourself constantly on guard, even in situations that didn’t used to bother you?

Yes. Especially around traffic. If I’m near a road, I’m watching every truck, every curb, every person crossing like it’s my job to spot something before it goes wrong.

It’s exhausting, and I know I didn’t used to be that way.
How long have you been feeling this way since your friend’s death? Have these feelings been constant, or have they changed over time?

It’s been going on since she was killed on that walking tour. That was about two years and three months ago now.

It’s changed some, I suppose, but it hasn’t really gone away. It’s just been there in one form or another since then.
